title: {Syn} Euler Phi Counts Units Modulo n
content:
Euler phi of n counts the positive integers up to n that are coprime to n. For a prime p, phi(p) equals p - 1 because every nonzero residue is invertible.

The function appears in Euler theorem, RSA, and many counting arguments where multiplication modulo n matters.

Why it matters: number theory keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
